yt-dlp._comment_v1.5.0: v1.5.0+ ships upstream's OFFICIAL Windows onedir build (yt-dlp_win.zip) byte-for-byte, fetched and SHA-256-verified by build/fetch-external-deps.ps1, and delivered to existing installs as bin/yt-dlp-pkg.zip (the official zip already has yt-dlp.exe + _internal/ at its root, which is exactly what src/YtDlpTool.Process/YtDlpLayout.cs expands). v1.3.0-v1.4.0 built a patched yt-dlp.exe from source instead; endpoint security (an endpoint-protection agent's behaviour monitoring) held that unknown, unsigned binary ~27s per launch and then refused it with 'Access denied', while the official build ran in under a second on the same machine. The AllowUntrustedCertificates workaround that the patch carried is now a yt-dlp plugin: src/YtDlpTool.Process/Plugins/ytdlptool_tls_relax.py. Do not go back to building yt-dlp yourself.
yt-dlp._comment_version: `version` MUST equal what `yt-dlp --version` prints: UpdateChecker compares the two, so any drift produces a permanent 'update available' prompt. fetch-external-deps.ps1 enforces this.
